parsed.rationale: All four members are `type-alias-object` declarations with empty `fields_or_signature` lists, meaning the structural signal is limited to the alias declaration shape itself rather than any meaningful shared logic. The names `LargeNowPlayingWidgetEntryView`, `MediumNowPlayingWidgetEntryView`, `SmallNowPlayingWidgetEntryView`, and `Header` are intentionally distinct widget-size variants and a layout sub-component living in separate files under `WXYC/iOS/NowPlayingWidget/Views/`. Type aliases for SwiftUI widget entry views are conventionally size-specific by WidgetKit design (Small/Medium/Large families), so their structural coincidence is an artifact of the alias pattern, not a refactor opportunity. No restraint markers are present, but collapsing these into a single shared alias would break the per-family customization contract that WidgetKit expects.
